correctness.rationale: PASS. Beta integrals give Jacobi E[X²]=tau=1/(2alpha+3), which bijectively ranges (0,1) for alpha>-1. Existence of prescribed nonnegative degree-two weights is equivalent to (0,tau) lying in the convex hull of (Xi,Xi²), i.e. product of closest opposite-sign absolute nodes ≤tau≤product of extremes, with strict all-node weights almost surely for m≥3. Exact order-statistic densities lead to the stated m-integral and P3=3tau(log(1/tau)-1+tau)/2; an independent symbolic integration reproduced this. Two boundary Laplace endpoints give outer 2/(1-tau)[(1+tau)/2]^m; the interior central gap maximum at sqrt(tau) gives sqrt(pi sqrt(tau)/[2(1-sqrt(tau))])*sqrt(m)*(1-sqrt(tau))^m. Equal bases solve tau=3-2sqrt2, hence alpha=sqrt2. The limit is pointwise fixed alpha; finite solver tests are corroborative only.
